symptoms: Acute onset illness involving skin/mucosa AND respiratory compromise, hypotension, or end-organ dysfunction
2 or more features after likely allergen exposure (skin/mucosa, respiratory, hypotension, GI symptoms)
Hypotension after exposure to known allergen (decline in SBP >= 30%)

management_steps.details: Stop/remove allergen. Position supine with legs elevated. High-flow O2, monitors, IV access. Administer ADRENALINE (1:1 000, 1mg/ml) 0.5 mls IM STAT anterolateral thigh (0.01mg/kg up to 0.5mg).
Nebulized Adrenaline (5mg) for partial airway obstruction. BVM for complete obstruction. Crystalloid (Ringers Lactate/Balsol) 20ml/kg IV bolus.
Promethazine (Phenergan) 12.5 mg slow IV (max 25mg; weight dependent in paeds). Hydrocortisone (Solucortef) 200 mg slow IV (weight dependent in paeds).
Repeat IM Adrenaline every 3-5 minutes or start Adrenaline infusion. In cardiac arrest: ACLS, adrenaline 3-5mg q2-3min + aggressive fluid volume.

warnings: Biphasic reaction occurs in 5-20% of cases. Observe patient closely.
